name: English
title: SHIN — Flexible ideas. Explicit authority.
description: An experimental language for websites, apps, CMS and AI workflows.
lead: Websites, applications, content and AI. Build different kinds of services with a language designed around clear permissions and checked data.
grant: Declared in code. Granted by the host.
mock: The demo provider echoes text; it is not an LLM.
deps_note: Runs on the Python 3.9+ standard library.
bytecode_note: A dedicated compiler and stack VM.
effects_note: The program cannot grant itself access.
website_body: Generate HTML with SHIN functions, then export a static website for your preferred host.
app_body: Build routes and JSON APIs. The starter app sends form input to SHIN and displays the calculated result.
cms_body: An authenticated editor and SQLite storage, with drafts, publication controls and conflict detection.
limits: Experimental release. Native app builds, user accounts, payments and multi-tenant CMS are not implemented. The bundled server is for local development.
requirements: You need Python 3.9+ and Git. The examples require no API key or model download.
local_model: For real AI inference, configure a separately running local Ollama server.
copy_failed: Select the commands and copy them manually.
open_local: After starting the server, open http://127.0.0.1:8000.
status_body: The compiler, VM, web toolkit and CMS are available under the MIT license. Tests and reproducible benchmarks are included.
performance: The Python reference VM is slower than Python on the included simple-loop benchmark. Native/Wasm execution and stronger isolation remain future work. Structural checks do not establish factual truth, and logical size budgets are not OS memory isolation.
community_title: Built in the open. Improved together.
community_body: SHIN is open source under the MIT license. Help with code, translations, documentation, examples or bug reports. First-time contributors are welcome.
